metaTitle: Sliding Glass Door Repair Plantation FL | Older Doors
description: Sliding glass door repair in Plantation: matching parts on one-of-a-kind older doors, clearing leaf-clogged tracks, and what the city asks for a new door.
h1: Sliding glass door repair in Plantation
subline: In a city planned so neighboring homes don't match, we size rollers and handles to your door and say when the frame is finished.
answer: Sliding glass door repair in Plantation usually comes down to rollers, the track or the lock, fixed inside the existing frame. Because neighboring homes here were built not to match, parts are matched by measurement. If the frame is badly damaged, replacement needs a city permit and a door approved for Broward's High-Velocity Hurricane Zone.
faqHeading: Questions Plantation homeowners ask about their sliders
closing: Send us a photo of your door and any label on the frame edge, or call, and we'll tell you whether it's a parts job or a frame problem.

faqs.q: Who can pull a door replacement permit in Plantation?
faqs.a: A licensed contractor registered with the City of Plantation, or the homeowner as an owner-builder. The city says owner-builders must meet with the plan reviewer before applying for any permit, and the product needs Miami-Dade or Florida approval.

faqs.q: Does a Plantation building permit mean my HOA has approved the new door?
faqs.a: No. The city states that issuing a building permit doesn't mean the work is approved by a condo, homeowners or property owners association. Get the association's approval separately, ideally in writing, before ordering a replacement door.

faqs.q: Does the year my Plantation house was built matter for a new door?
faqs.a: Yes, it can. Broward is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and the Florida Building Code lets one- and two-family homes built under codes before September 1, 1994 replace up to 25% of their glazed openings in 12 months without impact protection. The building department confirms.

faqs.q: Can you find rollers for an old aluminum slider with no brand label?
faqs.a: Often, yes. We measure the old roller's wheel, housing and mounting and match it to what's still made. Some discontinued doors have no compatible part left, and when that leaves the panel unable to roll properly, replacement becomes the honest answer.

faqs.q: Do leaves from shade trees really affect a sliding door?
faqs.a: Yes. Leaves, seed pods and grit collect in the sill track and clog the weep holes that drain it. Water then sits in the track and the rollers grind through debris. Vacuuming the track and brushing out the drain slots regularly helps.
